Tseitin's parity formula on the 3-regular graph with p = 5: 10 vertices, 15 edge atoms and 40 constraints, four per vertex, with an odd total charge. Summing the vertex equations counts every edge twice, so no choice of edges satisfies them.
The constraints form a linear system over GF(2) that elimination refutes in polynomial time; resolution needs exponentially many steps on expanding graphs as p grows.

Two parity chains over the inputs x(1..5), the second in the order of the permutation (I + 1)^3 + 7 mod 5: 13 atoms and 34 constraints. Both chains compute the exclusive-or of every input, so their results cannot differ.
The constraints form a linear system over GF(2) that elimination refutes in polynomial time; resolution needs exponentially many steps as p grows.

Five pigeons and four holes as clauses over 20 choice atoms: one constraint per pigeon that it occupies no hole and one per pair of pigeons sharing a hole, 45 in all.
Counting the incidences once by pigeon and once by hole refutes the conditions at once; resolution needs exponentially many steps as the holes grow.
